blocks.text: When a body is executing simple harmonic motion, it possesses both potential energy as well as kinetic energy. Its potential energy is on account of its displacement from mean position and the kinetic energy is due to its velocity. These energies vary during the oscillation, but the total energy at any instant remains constant in the absence of unbalanced frictional forces. In case of mass-spring system shown in Fig (14.10), when the mass is displaced from the mean position O then there is a restoring force (F) whose value is zero at mean position when x = 0 and its value is maximum at either extreme position where x = x₀. blocks.text: Eq. (14.29) should read T.E = ½mω²x₀²: putting k = mω² into ½kx₀² replaces k; it does not multiply by it.

From Eqs. (14.23), (14.27) and (14.28), it is proved that total energy of mass spring system is constant and is directly proportional to the square of the amplitude of oscillation. This statement of conservation of energy is equally valid for all bodies executing S.H.M. When K.E. of mass is maximum, mass passes through the centre of oscillation, the P.E. of mass spring is zero (x = 0), conversely when the P.E. of spring is maximum, the mass is at its extreme position on either side, the K.E. of mass is zero (x = x₀).
The energy oscillates between K.E. and P.E., but their sum remains constant. This can be illustrated by plotting graph of K.E., P.E. and T.E. verses displacement as shown in Fig. (14.11).

blocks.title: Example 14.5
blocks.problem: A body of 0.010 kg executes simple harmonic motion of period 6 s. one second after it has passed its mean position, it's velocity is 0.06 meter per second. Find its kinetic energy, potential energy and Total energy.
steps:
m = 0.010 kg
T = 6 s
v = 0.06 m s⁻¹ (at t = 1 s)

Angular frequency (ω)
ω = 2π/T = 2π/6 = π/3 rad s⁻¹

To find the total energy (Eᴛ), first, find the amplitude x₀, using the formula of velocity;
v = x₀ω sin(ωt)
0.06 m s⁻¹ = x₀(π/3) sin(π/3 × 1)
0.06 m s⁻¹ = x₀(π/3)(0.866)
0.06 m s⁻¹ = x₀(1.047)(0.866)
0.06 m s⁻¹ = 0.90x₀
x₀ = 0.066 m

Total energy Eᴛ of system is given by
Eᴛ = ½mω²x₀²

Substituting the values, we have:
Eᴛ = ½ 0.01(π/3)²(0.066)²
Eᴛ = 2.4 10⁻⁵ J

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The question times the motion from the mean position, but the solution uses v = x₀ω sin(ωt), which times it from an extreme position. From the mean position x = x₀ sin ωt and v = x₀ω cos ωt, so 0.06 m s⁻¹ = x₀(π/3) cos(π/3) = x₀(1.047)(0.5), giving x₀ ≈ 0.115 m. Then Eᴛ = ½mω²x₀² ≈ 7.2 × 10⁻⁵ J and P.E. = Eᴛ − K.E. ≈ 5.4 × 10⁻⁵ J; K.E. = 1.8 × 10⁻⁵ J is unchanged.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.text:
(i) P.E. can also be calculated by expression P.E. = ½kx² = ½mω²x² where x being displacement of a particle which can be found out by x = x₀ cosω t.
(ii) The total energy of a system can also be found out by Eᴛ = K.E. + P.E.
